title: The theatre circuit and the Deluxe record date
summary: After Baltimore, Washington and Philadelphia theatres, the band records for Deluxe, whose cardboard-like disks he dislikes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then we had engagements around. We played the Apollo Theatre... At that particular time you had a circuit that you played. You played the Apollo Theatre, you played the Royal Theatre in Baltimore, the Howard Theatre in Washington, D.C., and there was a couple of theatres in Philadelphia that you played. So we went on that circuit, played those theatres, and came back to New York and played some different engagements around New Jersey and Connecticut.
But we stuck around New York because we had a record date

coming up, our first record date. We had this date for what I felt was one of the worst record companies I ever recorded for. The records that they produced were like cardboard. If you played the disk, oh, four or five times, it was like you'd had it a hundred years. Because it was during the war, material was very bad. But I don't think it was ever an excuse to have material that bad. Anyway, this was Deluxe Record Company. We went in the studio and recorded six sides, I believe.
